rules.rule: No full message body, raw segment, field value or payload-carrying exception may reach a log call at INFO or above, an audit row, an alert, or an HTTP error body. Text from a directory, IdP or remote peer stays out of audit rows and refusal text too. Masking reuses an existing masker, for example messagefoundry/anon, messagefoundry/redaction.py, messagefoundry/support/redact.py or mask_for_display in messagefoundry/api/field_authz.py. Flag a new ad hoc masker written beside them.

SQL values are always bound parameters. Flag any f-string, % or .format() that puts a variable into SQL text unless the variable is an identifier or fragment chosen from a fixed in-code allowlist, and say which allowlist. A change to one store backend (sqlite, postgres, sqlserver) that alters a query's meaning must make the same change in the other backends.

Every new or changed HTTP or WebSocket route is gated in one of the sanctioned ways: a gate dependency marked with mark_route_gate in messagefoundry/api/security.py (the require* and require_ui* factories are marked this way); @public_route(reason); or, on a WebSocket only, @authorizes_in_body(reason) with the caller authorized in the handler before the socket is accepted and re-authorized before each later frame. Do not flag those forms as missing a gate. Flag a route with none of them; mark_route_gate applied to a dependency that does not enforce authentication; a new public_route whose reason is not a step before a session exists or is verified, for example sign-in, sign-out, second factor, re-authentication, liveness or a browser report; any public_route, new or existing, whose change makes it return or change operator, message or configuration data such as connection names, users or the version; and an authorizes_in_body WebSocket that accepts the socket or sends a frame before its authorization check succeeds. A route that returns or changes channel data filters by the caller's channel scope. Flag a change that discloses more about withheld items than the route already does by design, such as a new count, name or id. A state-changing admin action that the surrounding routes protect with step-up re-auth or dual-control approval needs the same protection.

A security decision fails closed. An exception, timeout, busy pool, unreachable directory or unexpected reply is an outage or fault, never 'no such user', 'wrong password', 'not revoked' or success. An unknown scheme tag, digest marker or enum value in a security decision is refused, not defaulted. Flag any branch where an error path lets a request through or reports a negative answer. This applies to authentication, authorization, revocation, TLS and secret handling. Tolerant HL7 parsing (ADR 0054) is not a security decision; do not apply this rule to it.

A write that grants, revokes or changes an account, factor, session or role re-reads the current record (or uses a guarded conditional write) in the same transaction. Flag check-then-write on state another request or process can change in between.

No connection sends a credential, token or PHI to a peer whose certificate and name were not verified, and no escape or opt-out permits it (docs/SECURITY-LOOSENING.md). Flag verify=False, CERT_NONE, check_hostname=False or a disabled CRL check on such a hop. On a hop that carries none of those, weakened TLS must be gated by weakened_tls_escape_permitted_here() in messagefoundry/config/settings.py and log at WARNING; flag one that bypasses that gate. An explicit context=None does not always verify: for stdlib smtplib, ftplib, imaplib and poplib starttls or *_TLS, None builds an unverified context. Flag None there.

Every received message ends with a recorded disposition. A bad message goes to the error or dead-letter path; it never ends the listener or worker, and it is never accepted and dropped. Parse with the built-in tolerant parser or the codec, read separators from MSH, and never edit raw HL7 by slicing, split('|') or replace before sending it on.

A security-relevant decision (sign-in, sign-out, refusal, revoke, role or factor change, PHI read, config write, approval) writes an audit row with the acting user. A failed audit write is handled explicitly and does not abort unrelated work or pass silently.

Anything that grows from outside input has a cap or deadline: caches, dedupe sets, rate-limiter buckets, paged directory searches, read loops on sockets or files, and retry loops. Flag a new collection or loop with no size cap, eviction or overall deadline.
